newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty idles at resistance, depos inch up.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty idles at resistance, depos inch up.

text.p: The Polish zloty settled in just below key resistance at 1.5 percent from parity on Monday without much impetus to seek higher ground or slip lower.
Dealers said the zloty would probably remain idle around resistance for the rest of Monday's session with no large-scale entry into Polish T-bills expected at today's primary tender.
"There is not much interest on the market, just closing client orders, and we should remain at 1.5 percent from parity for some time," said Pawel Gajewski, forex dealer at Creditanstalt in Warsaw.
At 0845 GMT the zloty was at 1.49/1.47 percent from parity, against opening's 1.51/1.49 percent and Friday's 1.53/1.49.
It was at 3.2410/17 to the dollar, up from 3.2420/30 at 0700 GMT and at 1.8761/66 to the mark, down from 1.8745/50.
Dealers said foreign investors were cautious on taking new positions in zloty-instruments in lieu of minute upside potential for the Polish zloty and no interest rate cut hopes.

On Saturday Gazeta Wyborcza daily quoted central banker Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz as saying that if credit growth was excessive in the next two months, the central bank may raise rates to cool domestic demand and consequently imports.
Dealers said a slight selling trend was felt in secondary T-bill trade ahead of Monday's primary auction, where yields were expected to rise, with foreigners mostly observing.
On the money market one-day rates inched up as the market tightened amid monthly tax payments during the last week of trade in June's required reserve period, which ends on Sunday.
At 0900 GMT overnight rates were quoted at 22.05/22.30 percent, up from 21.90/22.20 at 0636 GMT and tomorrow/next were at 22.00/22.36 percent against 21.90/22.20.
